thought_title: Antony shared every suffering and lived wholly for heaven
orientation: Hesychius keeps applying words from Hebrews to Antony and then ends the homily with a call to imitate him by the grace of Christ.
pass_a_gloss: But further also he was beaten with a club, he died by murder of a sword, he took trial of bonds and of prison and of whips, he was stoned, he was sawn asunder; for while many suffered these things because of reverence toward God, he himself as father of all suffered together with all; he went about in cloaks of sheep, in skins of goats, while imitating Elijah in meekness; while being in want in the flesh and while being afflicted, for he knew that afflictions are a road of the kingdom of the heavens; while being ill treated, because Antony wished rather to be ill treated together with the people of God than to have temporary enjoyment of sin; the world was not worthy of him; therefore while still living he transferred himself into heaven. Then let us pass through the great body of the prophets. Let Christ the head seal the praises in our hands, while saying still even now, the kingdom of the heavens is forceful and forceful men seize it; for Antony melted the body, he bridled the soul, he chastised pleasures, he kept away from luxury, he spared satiety, he used sleep only so much as to benefit nature, he judged even the mere name of sexual wrong to be abominable, he enjoyed few things of earth. And he was wholly toward heaven, wholly of the life above, while judging the things here to be loss. He lived by virtues alone, while being dead to passions. He held the foe as a plaything, the devil fell before his feet. Having taken courage he went up upon asp and basilisk, he trampled down the spiritual lion and dragon. He judged temptations to be gain, afflictions to be trading profit. He judged joy to be in mourning for sins, wealth to be in being poor. He had all things, because he had nothing. He was lord of all things; for he served no one. He looked down upon all things; for he needed nothing. May we also come into zeal for him, as many as have come together today in his festival of his holy commemoration, as many as marvel at his revered life and as many as celebrate his blessed falling asleep out of faith, by grace and love for humankind of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom to the Father be glory, honor, might with the Holy Spirit now and always and into the ages of the ages. Amen.

pass_b_english: Moreover, he too “was tortured,” “died by the sword,” “knew chains, prison, and scourgings,” “was stoned, was sawn apart” (Hebrews 11:35–37). Many endured these things for godliness, and Antony suffered with them all as the father of all. He “went about in sheepskins and goatskins” (Hebrews 11:37), copying Elijah in meekness. He was “in want” in the flesh and “afflicted” (Hebrews 11:37), because he knew that afflictions are the road to the kingdom of heaven. He was ill treated because he chose “to suffer with the people of God rather than enjoy sin for a season” (Hebrews 11:25). “The world was not worthy of him” (Hebrews 11:38). So while he still lived, Antony moved himself to heaven. Let us pass over the great crowd of the prophets.

Let Christ the head seal the praises in our hands. Even now he says, “The kingdom of heaven is taken by force, and forceful men seize it” (Matthew 11:12). Antony made his body waste away. He bridled his soul. He disciplined his pleasures. He kept clear of soft living. He refused excess. He allowed himself only enough sleep to sustain his nature. He counted even the word for sexual sin as hateful. He enjoyed little from the earth. He belonged wholly to heaven and wholly to the life above, and he counted the things here as loss. He lived by the virtues alone, for he was dead to the passions.

He made a plaything of his foe, and the devil fell at his feet. He took courage and “trod on the asp and the basilisk, and trampled the spiritual lion and the dragon underfoot” (Psalm 91:13). He counted temptations as gain and afflictions as profit. He found joy in mourning for sins and wealth in being poor. He possessed all things because he possessed nothing. He was lord over all things, for he served no one. He looked down on all things, for he needed nothing. May we come to share his zeal, all of us gathered today for the festival of his holy commemoration, all who admire his venerable life, and all who celebrate his blessed falling asleep in faith, by the grace and love of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom to the Father be glory, honor, and might, with the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.

problems.why: Greek uses third-person singular verbs applying Hebrews 11 directly to Antony, not plural 'they' spoken by Paul, and places the sheepskins clause after the sympathy explanation.
problems.fix: Moreover, he too “was tortured,” “died by the sword,” “knew chains, prison, and scourgings,” “was stoned, was sawn apart” (Hebrews 11:35–37).
problems.ruling: Source has singular «ἐτυμπανίσθη», «ἀπέθανε»; no Paul; «μηλωταῖς» follows «συνέπασχε», not first quote block.

problems.quote: Paul says they were “left in want, afflicted, and ill treated” (Hebrews 11:38).
problems.why: These participles are from Hebrews 11:37, not 11:38, and the Greek applies them directly to Antony in the singular rather than quoting Paul in the plural.
problems.fix: He was “in want” in his flesh and “afflicted” (Hebrews 11:37)
problems.ruling: «ὑστερούμενος» τῇ σαρκὶ, «θλιβόμενος» are singular Antony; text is 11:37, not 11:38.

problems.quote: “The kingdom of heaven is forceful, and forceful men seize it”
problems.why: The verbal adjective βιαστή is passive ('taken by force' or 'won by force'), not active ('forceful').
problems.fix: “The kingdom of heaven is taken by force, and forceful men seize it”
problems.ruling: «βιαστή ἐστι» is passive kingdom-under-violence, not active “forceful”; misquotes Matthew 11:12 sense.
